name: Italy
headline: Italy: +0.5% growth in 2025, 1.6% inflation, debt 137% of GDP
sections: Italy is a $2.55 trillion economy (2025), the world's 10th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $63K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 15.0% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.6% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.1% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 20.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 137% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 154% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.1% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +1.1% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 63% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 136% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 84.0 years (2024). Population: 58.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
